retention.title: Data Retention
retention.metricsScrapeDescription: McHarbor exposes its own metrics in Prometheus text format. Scrapers authenticate with an API key that carries the metrics.scrape permission.
retention.description: Configure how long audit logs and activity events are kept. Backup retention is configured on each container backup schedule. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.auditDaysDescription: Number of days to keep audit log entries. Older entries are automatically purged.
retention.activityDaysDescription: Number of days to keep container activity events. Older events are automatically purged.
retention.backupDaysDescription: Maximum number of days to keep successful backups per container. Older backup archives are deleted automatically. Set to 0 to keep backups regardless of age.
retention.backupCountDescription: Maximum number of successful backups to keep per container. Older backup archives are deleted automatically. Set to 0 to keep all backups.
retention.clearNowHint: Run the retention purge now (entries older than {{days}} days)
retention.clearAuditDescription: Permanently delete all audit log entries older than {{days}} days. The deleted count will be shown after the operation. This cannot be undone.
retention.clearActivityDescription: Permanently delete all activity events older than {{days}} days. The deleted count will be shown after the operation. This cannot be undone.
retention.keepForever: Set retention to a positive number to enable clearing.
retention.lifecycleDaysDescription: Days to keep lifecycle events before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.backupLogDaysDescription: Days to keep backup-log rows before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.scanDaysDescription: Days to keep vulnerability scans (and their findings) before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.clearLifecycleDescription: Permanently delete every lifecycle event older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.
retention.clearBackupLogDescription: Permanently delete every backup log row older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.
retention.clearScansDescription: Permanently delete every vulnerability scan (and its findings) older than {{days}} days. This action cannot be undone.
retention.auditPresetDescription: Pick a preset to apply a recommended audit retention period, or choose Custom to set your own.
retention.metricsRawHoursDescription: Hours to keep per-sample container metrics before they are rolled up. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.metricsRollupDaysDescription: Days to keep hourly metric rollups before the next purge. Set to 0 to keep forever.
retention.metricsDiskDescription: Sample container filesystem usage alongside CPU and memory. Adds load on hosts with many containers.
retention.recordExecDescription: Store the commands and output of terminal sessions opened from McHarbor.
retention.recordExecWarningBody: Anything typed or printed in a session is stored, including passwords and tokens. Keep the retention period short and restrict who may read the audit log.
retention.backupSectionDescription: How long backup log events are kept before they are purged. Set to 0 to keep forever.

agent.description: Configure how McHarbor communicates with remote agents. These settings affect event collection, heartbeat pings, metrics, and request timeouts for all agent-connected environments.

agent.eventPollIntervalDescription: How often to fetch new events from agent environments. Lower values mean more frequent updates but higher load.
agent.pingIntervalDescription: How often to send keepalive pings to connected agents.
agent.metricsEnabledDescription: Enable host metrics collection for agent environments. One-shot stats take ~2s per container through the agent transport.
agent.statsPushIntervalDescription: How often agents that support it push container stats. McHarbor stretches the interval for every agent when too many push at once.
agent.requestTimeoutDescription: Maximum time to wait for a response from the agent before timing out.

directTransferTest.title: Agent-to-agent transfer test
directTransferTest.description: Verify that one connected agent can reach another agent's direct transfer listener.
directTransferTest.dialogDescription: Direct transfer diagnostics for the selected source and target agents.
directTransferTest.notEnoughAgents: Connect at least two agents to run this test.
directTransferTest.requestFailed: The agent-to-agent transfer test request failed.

interpretation.receiverMissing: The request reached an agent listener that did not have the prepared one-use receiver. This usually means the advertised URL points to the wrong agent, a stale container, or a different process on the same port.
interpretation.bearerMissing: The receiver did not see the bearer authorization header. A proxy or network hop may be stripping Authorization, or the request did not come from the source-agent probe.
interpretation.tokenMismatch: The receiver saw a bearer token, but it did not match the prepared receiver token. This points to stale transfer state, duplicate agent processes, or a token correlation bug.
interpretation.noDiagnostic: The target agent did not report receiver diagnostics. The request may have reached an old or disconnected agent process, or the target agent is not running the diagnostic-capable version.
interpretation.wrongResponder: The HTTP responder marker does not match the prepared target marker. The advertised URL is reaching a different agent listener than the connected target agent.
interpretation.genericFailure: The receiver reported an authorization failure, but the diagnostic flags do not match a known case.

itsm.title: Ticket status from the ITSM
itsm.webhookHint: Give the ITSM this channel's inbound URL so it can tell McHarbor when a ticket is acknowledged or closed.
itsm.pollOnly: This ITSM is asked for ticket status on the channel's poll interval; no inbound URL is needed.
itsm.oneWay: This channel only sends to the ITSM. Tickets it opens show no status from the ITSM, and McHarbor resolves them when the alert recovers.
itsm.showOnce: Copy these now. They are not shown again; rotating issues new ones and breaks the old ones.
itsm.tokenSet: An inbound URL is set. Rotate to issue a new one.
itsm.vendorSecret: Signing secret issued by the ITSM

storage.description: Configure reusable external storage locations for backups, exports, and future storage workflows.
storage.backupKeyDescription: Generate a 32-byte key for the Docker secret mcharbor_backup_key. McHarbor only shows it once and does not store it.
storage.backupKeyGeneratedWarning: Copy or install this key now. McHarbor does not store generated backup keys, and replacing it later can make existing encrypted backups unreadable unless you keep the old key.
storage.regenerateBackupKeyDescription: This replaces the key currently shown here. Copy or install the current key first; McHarbor cannot show it again. If you install a new key, keep the old key or existing encrypted backups may become unreadable.
storage.backupKeyCopyOnceHint: Copy this key now, then store it as the mcharbor_backup_key Docker secret before running encrypted backups.
storage.selectTypeDescription: Choose the storage provider or protocol you want to configure.
storage.confirmDeleteDescription: This will permanently delete this storage location configuration.
storage.passiveModeDescription: Recommended for FTP/FTPS through NAT, but the server still needs a passive data-port range opened.
storage.ftpSecurityHint: FTP is the original protocol: credentials and files are sent in cleartext. It uses TCP 21 plus dynamic data ports, which is difficult through firewalls and NAT.
storage.ftpsSecurityHint: FTPS is classic FTP protected with SSL/TLS. It encrypts commands and data, but still uses FTP's multi-port active/passive data-channel behavior.
storage.sftpSecurityHint: SFTP is an SSH subsystem. It encrypts all data and authentication natively and uses one firewall-friendly TCP port, normally 22.
storage.ftpPortHint: Default control port is TCP 21. Data transfer may require TCP 20 or passive dynamic ports.
storage.ftpsPortHint: Explicit FTPS commonly uses TCP 21. Implicit FTPS commonly uses TCP 990. Passive data ports may also be required.
storage.sftpPortHint: Default SFTP port is TCP 22 and all traffic stays on this single port.
storage.ftpAuthHint: FTP sends username and password in cleartext unless FTPS is selected.
storage.privateKeyHint: Paste an OpenSSH private key. It is encrypted at rest and is not returned after saving.
storage.passphraseHint: Optional. Required only when the private key is passphrase-protected.
storage.caCertificateHint: Optional PEM CA certificate used to validate the FTPS server certificate.
storage.clientCertificateHint: Optional PEM client certificate for servers requiring mutual TLS.
storage.clientKeyHint: Optional PEM private key for the FTPS client certificate.
storage.secretHint: Leave blank to keep existing secret
storage.credentialsDescription: Credential fields are encrypted at rest and are not shown again after saving.
storage.consentDescription: Save this location, then use Connect to grant account consent. McHarbor stores the returned tokens encrypted.
storage.driveIdConsentHint: Optional. Leave blank to use the default drive returned by the provider.
storage.setupGuideDescription: Use these steps to prepare the provider before saving this storage location.

setupGuide.basePath: Set the base path where McHarbor should store backups and exported files.
setupGuide.localMount: Mount a host directory into the McHarbor container. The default compose mount maps MCHARBOR_LOCAL_BACKUP_PATH to /mnt/backup.
setupGuide.localPath: Set the local backup path. Use /mnt/backup unless you mounted a different container path.
setupGuide.localMountNative: Pick a directory on this host. McHarbor runs as a systemd service that may only write under /var/lib/mcharbor; any other directory needs a ReadWritePaths= drop-in for mcharbor.service.
setupGuide.localPathNative: Make the directory writable by the mcharbor user (sudo chown -R mcharbor:mcharbor <directory>) and enter its full path below.
setupGuide.localMountNativeRoot: Pick a directory on this host. McHarbor runs as root here, so any local path works without extra permissions.

storage.microsoftBusinessConsentDescription: Save this location, then use Connect to grant Microsoft 365 account consent. McHarbor stores the returned tokens encrypted.
storage.tenantIdConsentHint: Required. Use your Microsoft Entra tenant ID or verified tenant domain.
storage.enterBackupKeyDescription: Install an existing base64-encoded 32-byte backup key as the McHarbor Docker secret.
storage.enterBackupKeyHint: Use the original key for existing encrypted backups. Installing a different key can make older backups require their old secret during restore.
storage.installProjectPathHint: Required only when McHarbor runs outside Docker Compose. Leave empty to auto-detect from the container labels. Must be the host directory that contains docker-compose.yml.
storage.localPathHint: McHarbor writes to this path inside the container. Mount it to a host folder with MCHARBOR_LOCAL_BACKUP_PATH so the files live outside the container.
storage.localPathHelper: Default is /mnt/backup. The directory must be writable by the McHarbor container.
storage.localPathHelperNative: A directory on this host, writable by the mcharbor user. Outside /var/lib/mcharbor it also needs a ReadWritePaths= drop-in for mcharbor.service.
storage.localPathHelperNativeRoot: A directory on this host. McHarbor runs as root here, so no extra permissions are needed.
storage.typeLocalDescription: Store files on a host-mounted path available to the McHarbor container.
storage.encryptionRowDescription: Encrypts backup archives at rest with the mcharbor_backup_key Docker secret.
storage.encryptionRowDescriptionNative: Encrypts backup archives at rest with the backup key in /var/lib/mcharbor/secrets/mcharbor_backup_key.
storage.pluginOwnedFormHint: This storage type is provided by a plugin, which owns its own connection fields.

catalogs.title: Catalogs
catalogs.help: Catalogs are the sources McHarbor reads app and plugin definitions from. A source can be a remote index URL or a local directory.

transport.insecure: Read over plain HTTP; the payload can be tampered with in transit.

transport.untrustedInsecure: Third-party source read over plain HTTP. Its entries are neither authenticated nor protected in transit.
transport.untrustedPlugin: Third-party plugin source. Plugins run code inside McHarbor, so only add sources you trust.
transport.untrustedPluginInsecure: Third-party plugin source read over plain HTTP. Plugins run code inside McHarbor, so this combination is best avoided.

backupKey.title: Backup encryption key
backupKey.generatedWarning: Copy or install this key now. McHarbor does not store generated backup keys, and replacing it later can make existing encrypted backups unreadable unless you keep the old key.
backupKey.copyOnceHint: Copy this key now, then store it as the mcharbor_backup_key Docker secret before running encrypted backups.
backupKey.enterDescription: Paste a backup encryption key you already hold. McHarbor installs it as the mcharbor_backup_key secret and restarts.
backupKey.enterHint: The key is used as-is; McHarbor never stores a copy of it.
backupKey.installProjectPathHint: Only needed when the compose project lives somewhere McHarbor cannot infer.
backupKey.description: Generate a 32-byte key for the Docker secret mcharbor_backup_key. McHarbor only shows it once and does not store it.

native.description: Generate a 32-byte backup encryption key. On this native install McHarbor keeps it in its data directory and restarts to load it. It is shown only once.
native.copyOnceHint: Copy this key now and keep it safe: restoring an encrypted backup needs it. Install and restart puts it in the data directory; the command above does the same from a shell on the host.
native.enterDescription: Paste a backup encryption key you already hold. McHarbor writes it to its data directory and restarts to load it.

backupKey.regenerateDescription: A new key replaces the current one. Backups encrypted with the old key stay unreadable unless you keep that key. This cannot be undone.

passwordPolicy.title: Password policy
passwordPolicy.description: Tune the password policy enforced on user-create, password-reset, and admin-set flows. Changes apply immediately on save.
passwordPolicy.minLengthHint: Used for new passwords, admin-set, and email reset flows.
passwordPolicy.maxAgeHint: 0 disables forced rotation. Affects users on next login.
passwordPolicy.historySizeHint: Reject reuse of any of the last N previous passwords. 0 disables history check.
passwordPolicy.invalidMinLength: Minimum length must be at least {{min}} characters.

contact.title: Contact us
contact.intro: Questions, licensing enquiries, bug reports and feature requests all reach the McHarbor maintainers through one of the channels below.

email.title: General & licensing
email.description: Commercial licensing, partnerships, and anything that does not belong in a public issue.

issues.title: Bug reports & feature requests
issues.description: Open an issue on GitHub. Include the diagnostics below so the report can be reproduced.

website.title: Documentation & releases
website.description: Release notes, guides, and the current documentation for every McHarbor version.

security.title: Reporting a security issue
security.description: Email {{address}} with SECURITY in the subject line rather than opening a public issue, so the problem can be fixed before it is described in the open.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: Paste this into your message. It carries version and platform details only — no tokens, hostnames, or container data.

branding.title: Application logo
branding.description: Replace the McHarbor mark with your own. It is shown in the sidebar and on the login page for everyone. Each mark takes an optional dark-theme version.
branding.usingDefault: No custom image uploaded — the McHarbor mark is shown.
branding.tooLarge: Image is too large. The limit is {{size}} KB.
branding.wrongType: Unsupported image type. Use SVG, PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF.
branding.wideLightDescription: Shown in the expanded sidebar and on the login card. A wide image works best.
branding.wideDarkDescription: Used in dark mode. Leave empty to reuse the light-theme wordmark.
branding.iconLightDescription: Shown on the collapsed sidebar rail, where a wordmark does not fit. A square image works best.
branding.iconDarkDescription: Used in dark mode. Leave empty to reuse the light-theme icon.

hostUpdates.title: Host OS packages
hostUpdates.selfSubtitle: Pending package updates on the machine McHarbor is installed on. This page always acts on that host, whatever environment is selected.
hostUpdates.warningTitle: This changes the host, not McHarbor
hostUpdates.warningBody: Applying updates runs the host's package manager. It can restart services, pull in a new kernel, and take the machine down for a reboot. Run it in a maintenance window, not on a whim.

agentReleases.title: Agent releases
agentReleases.subtitle: Every agent install and update is served from these. McHarbor downloads them from the sources below and verifies each against its signed SHA256SUMS before storing it.
agentReleases.noTarget: No target is selected: agents are served the locally built agent, else the one bundled with this McHarbor.
agentReleases.latestUnknown: No release check has run yet.
agentReleases.empty: No agent releases are stored yet.
agentReleases.deleteDescription: Its binaries and images are removed from McHarbor. It can be downloaded again later from any source that still has it.
agentReleases.imageErrorTitle: Why the agent image was not stored

settings.title: Agent release downloads
settings.subtitle: Where McHarbor looks for new agent versions, when, and what it does when it finds one.
settings.enabledHint: Runs on the schedule below. Agents are only ever served what McHarbor has stored.
settings.mode: When a new release is found
settings.modeHint: A new target reaches agents through the agent auto-update and its install window, or through Update all.

modes.rollout: Download it and make it the target

settings.keepHint: Older releases are removed after each download, except the target and any version a connected agent runs.
settings.sourcesHint: The official GitHub releases, or an HTTPS mirror laid out as the documentation describes. Whichever source serves a release, it must verify against the signing key pinned in McHarbor.
settings.imagePlatformsHint: Container agents load their replacement image from McHarbor. It is pulled from the digest a release signs, else from this repository at the release version.

hostServices.title: Host services
hostServices.selfSubtitle: systemd services on the machine McHarbor is installed on. This page always acts on that host, whatever environment is selected.
hostServices.warningTitle: This changes the host, not McHarbor
hostServices.warningBody: Stopping, disabling or reconfiguring a service here acts on the machine McHarbor runs on. McHarbor's own units and its container runtime can be restarted but not stopped or disabled.
